disclaimer: Scope: analyses are derived from orbital remote-sensing and model products. Traverses are simulated candidates on a documented cost model; water-ice results are relative investigation priorities, not detections. Results support, and do not replace, mission certification and in-situ confirmation.

dataset.title: SYNTHETIC demo terrain (not lunar data)
dataset.region_note: Procedurally generated craters on a 12.8 km square. Does not describe any real location.

elevation.crs: IAU Moon south polar stereographic (R=1737.4 km)

psr_mask.crs: IAU Moon south polar stereographic (R=1737.4 km)

thermal_max.crs: IAU Moon south polar stereographic (R=1737.4 km)

elevation.title: Elevation
elevation.method: Block-mean 2x2 of source DEM (cells need >=75% valid sub-pixels).
limitations: Gridded from altimetry tracks; interpolated between tracks (see effective resolution).
Heights are relative to a sphere, not a geoid.

hillshade.title: Hillshade (visual aid)
limitations: Not a simulation of real lunar illumination; polar sun is near the horizon.

slope.title: Slope
slope.method: Horn (1981) finite differences on the analysis grid; NaN propagates from no-data.
limitations: Baseline 160 m: slopes at rover-wheel scale can be steeper.
Polar stereographic scale error <= 0.001% ignored.

roughness.title: Roughness (detrended RMS)
roughness.method: Least-squares plane removal per window (separable correlation).
limitations: Scale-dependent; sub-cell roughness (boulders) is not captured.

psr.title: Permanently shadowed regions
psr.method: Block mean of the producer's 0/1 PSR map (illumination modelling on LOLA topography).
limitations: Model of illumination over the modelled epoch; small PSRs below grid scale are smoothed.

thermal_max.title: Annual max temperature (SYNTHETIC)
thermal_max.method: Thermal-model fit (PDS PRP) resampled nearest-facet then block-averaged.
limitations: Model product fitted to the first year of Diviner data; native facet spacing is coarser than this grid.
A single temperature does not describe sub-facet conditions (micro cold traps).

thermal_avg.title: Annual mean temperature, 2 cm depth (Diviner PRP)
limitations: not provided

ice_stability_depth.title: Ice stability depth (Diviner PRP)
limitations: not provided by this dataset

hydrogen.title: LEND hydrogen
limitations: not provided by this dataset

hazard.title: Mobility hazard class
hazard.method: Slope edges [10.0, 15.0, 25.0] deg, blocked >= 25.0 deg; roughness high >= 2.0 m, blocked >= 6.0 m.
limitations: PROTOTYPE thresholds, not a certified rover specification.
Unknown cells (no data) are never classed as safe.

cost.title: Traversal cost multiplier
limitations: Relative cost; not energy or time.
Weights are prototype assumptions.

priority_score.title: Ice investigation priority (score)
limitations: Investigation priority, NOT detection of water ice.
Weights are explicit prototype choices; see sensitivity.
Layers missing: ice_stability_depth, hydrogen.

priority_class.title: Ice investigation priority (class)
limitations: Investigation priority, NOT detection of water ice.
Weights are explicit prototype choices; see sensitivity.
Layers missing: ice_stability_depth, hydrogen.

priority_sensitivity.title: Priority sensitivity (std)
limitations: High values: ranking depends on weight choices.

boulder_detection.reason: grid is 80 m/px; rover-scale boulders (<10 m) are sub-pixel. Requires native-resolution NAC/ShadowCam imagery (~0.5–2 m/px) and a labelled training/evaluation set.

ice_investigation_priority.wording: Relative investigation priority from available evidence. Not a detection of water ice.

route.label: Simulated candidate route — not mission-certified
route.cost_semantics: Path cost = sum over moves of step length x mean per-metre cost multiplier of the two cells; a value equal to the length means flat, certain, low-hazard terrain all the way. Relative units — not energy, time or risk probability.

assumptions: Slope classes [10.0, 15.0, 25.0] deg and blocked >= 25.0 deg are prototype assumptions.
Roughness high >= 2.0 m, blocked >= 6.0 m RMS (prototype).
Cost weights {'slope': 8.0, 'roughness': 3.0, 'uncertainty': 4.0, 'psr': 1.5} are prototype choices; cost is relative, not energy or time.
Ground distance equals grid distance (polar stereographic scale error < 0.04 % within 2 deg of the pole).
No-data and unknown cells are treated as blocked for routing.
limitations: SYNTHETIC DATA: this report does not describe any real lunar location.
Analysis grid 80.0 m/px: rover-scale obstacles (boulders, small craters) are not resolved.
PSR map, temperatures and ice-stability depth are model products, each with its own epoch and resolution.
No LEND hydrogen layer was used; no direct measurement of water ice is included.
Illumination, communications line-of-sight and thermal survival are not modelled in the route.

summary.hotel_power_source: derived: 5420 Wh / 9 h - flat-drive mobility 22.7 W

rover.name: NASA VIPER (Volatiles Investigating Polar Exploration Rover)
references: Bluethmann, VIPER Rover Overview and Mobility and Hardware, LSIC 2024-11-14 (docs/references/viper_lsic2024_mobility_hw.pdf)
Schepelmann et al. 2025, PSJ, VIPER mobility (docs/references/viper_mobility_psj2025.pdf)

track_width_m.src: ~1.3 m at nominal ride height, Schepelmann et al. 2025

psr_ops_limit_h.src: batteries sized for 9 h shadowed operations

cg_height_m.src: centre-of-mass height not published; assumed 0.75 m (body + mast)

drive_efficiency.src: motor x gearbox x electronics efficiency, not published

hotel_power_w.src: calibrated so a flat drive at nominal speed exhausts 5420 Wh in the published 9 h PSR limit

battery_reserve_frac.src: operational reserve not published; 10 % kept in reserve

max_slip_ops.src: slip-sinkage expected to be controlled under 40 % slip, Schepelmann et al. 2025

soil.name: Lunar regolith — Apollo LRV design values
soil.src: Costes, Farmer & George (1972) Mobility performance of the Lunar Roving Vehicle; Carrier (1991) Lunar Sourcebook ch. 9; as quoted in Carrier, LGI 'Trafficability of lunar microrovers' Part 1 (docs/references/lgi_trafficability_part1.pdf)

fidelity: Terrain is the LOLA DEM at its native 20 m grid (bilinear). Rocks, boulders and craters smaller than ~20-40 m are invisible to this simulation; VIPER's published 15 cm obstacle limit cannot be checked from this data.
Wheel-soil forces use the Bekker-Wong model with Apollo LRV soil parameters (Costes et al. 1972). Real PSR regolith properties are unmeasured and may differ; see the loose-soil sensitivity run.
Quasi-static model: no dynamics, wheel-level suspension articulation, slip-sinkage or turn-in-place time.
Solar and Earth visibility are long-term AVERAGES (Mazarico et al. 2011), not a time-specific illumination simulation.
Parameters tagged 'assumed' are not published by the agency and are shown in the parameter table.
